**Finding submitted — deviation (IP, critical).**

- **Where:** §10.4 Development of Custom Software (p0185), read with §17.2 M&I Systems (p0244).
- **Problem:** M&I takes ownership of every work of authorship it creates "even if paid for by Customer," and §17.2 leaves us with no rights in M&I software or modifications except use "during the Term." We therefore neither own the deliverables we fund (preferred) nor hold a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense them (fallback). The Article 23 source-code escrow doesn't cure this — it is contingent and expires with the Term.
- **Not flagged:** §17.1 (we remain sole owner of Customer Data) is favourable; M&I retaining its platform and generic know-how is acceptable.
- **Redline (validated ok:true):** Customer-funded Developed Software becomes our property with an express assignment; M&I keeps pre-existing/generic tools and know-how and grants a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to any of its materials embedded in that work; M&I may still resell Developed Software we did not pay for; §17.2 is disapplied to these rights. Fallback (licence-only) offered in the comment.
